calls.reason: A blinded clinician study found GPT-5 Auto still gave inappropriate replies to psychotic prompts at greatly raised rates. OpenAI itself admits failures remain in sensitive conversations. The claim was 'not reliably', not 'never'.
The forecast is about what historians will write in 2043. That year has not come, and the packet has no qualifying retrospectives.
OpenAI's dated announcement shows GPT-5 came out on August 7, 2025, eleven days after the post. That fits 'about to drop', which he said with emphatic confidence.
The evidence is thin: one arithmetic benchmark at 97% accuracy and a small Ars Technica test with mixed results. Neither shows how often obvious errors happen or how hard they are to predict.

OpenAI's disclosure and several studies back his near-term GPT-4 warnings: hallucinations, bias and medical errors. But some of the seven predictions run to 2033 and 2043, and function calling partly cuts against the downstream-use prediction.

Epoch shows big benchmark gains. Spatial, proof and social-reasoning studies find recurring GPT-5 failures, especially on complex multi-stage tasks and when the context shifts. That is the mix he predicted.
